text:
**Yes, but only some models, and it depends on your computer.** A power station that just has AC outlets can cut power to your PC during an outage. One that is built to act as a UPS can carry it through.

**What to check**
- **Documented UPS/EPS mode with automatic switchover.** Anker says a basic power station may keep appliances running but still interrupt a computer during an outage. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups))
- **Transfer time.** EcoFlow calls this the #1 factor and warns that 20-30 ms switchovers can risk data loss. ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)) Anker notes that even 10 or 20 ms is not 0 ms, so check your device's manual. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)) Both are selling these products, and EcoFlow's claim that 9 out of 10 won't work is marketing language. Many desktop power supplies tolerate brief gaps, but I'd test rather than assume.
- **Pure sine wave output**, which suits computers and monitors.
- **Enough continuous watts** for your PC and monitor, measured at the wall with a plug-in watt meter.
- **Pass-through use** confirmed in the manual, with good ventilation.

**Runtime estimate:** watt-hours × ~0.85 ÷ load in watts. For example, a 1,000 Wh unit running a 100 W load lasts about 8.5 hours at best. Real-world runtime will be shorter. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups))

**Options from these results**
- **[EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)**: 600 W output and a switchover under 10 ms, which EcoFlow says is enough for a desktop and external drives. It's a good fit for a typical home PC.
- **[Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)**: 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W pure sine wave output and a 10 ms UPS switchover. It was listed at $699.99 after coupon, but that is a promotional price that may have changed. It suits a longer runtime or a bigger setup.
- I'd skip EcoFlow's DELTA line unless you check the specs. EcoFlow's blog lists the DELTA Pro 3 as ">10ms" UPS, and I couldn't confirm switching times for the [DELTA 3 Classic](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/delta-3-classic-portable-power-station/support) from the search results.

**When to buy a regular UPS instead:** if your PC or NAS manual requires 0 ms transfer, or you need standard UPS communication for automatic shutdown, an online double-conversion UPS is the safer choice. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas))

If you tell me your PC's wattage and how long you want it to run, I can narrow this to one model.
